The reason that Peters’ behaviour could destroy the coalition’s chances of re-election is not because people feel sorry for his treatment of Chinese-born MP Lawrence Xu-Nan, or because Peters has behaved like a fringe-dwelling thug instead of an elder statesman, or because he has clearly ignored the national interest in defending his indefensible comments.

While all of those are true, the most immediate political effect of Peters’ recent behaviour over matters related to China and India is that it has seriously undermined trust between parties and personnel within the Government.
